verses.text: God in his mercy has given us this work to do, so we do not give up.

We have turned away from secret and shameful ways. We do not use tricks, and we do not twist God's message. Instead, we tell the truth plainly, and so we show everyone's conscience in front of God what kind of people we are.
If the good news we preach is covered by a veil, it is covered only for those who are dying.
The god of this world has blinded the minds of those who do not believe. So they cannot see the light of the good news about the glory of Christ, who is the image of God.
We do not preach about ourselves. We preach that Jesus Christ is Lord, and that we are your servants for Jesus' sake.
God said, "Let light shine out of darkness." He is the one who has made his light shine in our hearts. He lets us know the glory of God that we see in the face of Jesus Christ.
But we have this treasure in jars made of clay. This shows that the great power comes from God, and not from us.
We have troubles on every side, but we are not crushed. We are confused, but we do not give up hope.
People attack us, but God does not leave us. We are knocked down, but we are not destroyed.
We always carry in our bodies the death of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus can also be seen in our bodies.
While we live, we are always being handed over to death for Jesus' sake, so that his life can be seen in our bodies that die.
So death is at work in us, but life is at work in you.
It is written, "I believed, so I spoke." We have the same spirit of faith. We also believe, and so we speak.
We know that God, who raised the Lord Jesus from death, will also raise us with Jesus. He will bring us, together with you, to stand in front of him.
All this is for your good. As God's grace reaches more and more people, more and more people will thank God, and that brings him glory.
So we do not give up. Our bodies are wearing out, but inside we are being made new day by day.
Our troubles are small, and they last only a short time. But they are bringing us a glory that lasts for ever, a glory far greater than all our troubles.
So we do not look at what can be seen, but at what cannot be seen. What can be seen lasts only a short time, but what cannot be seen lasts for ever.
